layers.note: A tall herb in patches in wet meadows, seeps, stream banks and avalanche tracks.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; often cool, wet hollows.

elevation_m.note: Near sea level in Alaska to subalpine in the Cascades.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −20 to 4 °C; gone below −30 °C and above 8 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −42 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −50 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 8 to 22 °C; gone below 6 °C, where summers are too short, and above 26 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 700 to 5,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 400.

degree_days_5.note: About 200 to 3,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 80.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.55, gone by 0.4.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Green false hellebore grows from Alaska through British Columbia to Oregon and northern California, east to Montana, and in eastern North America (general range knowledge; not checked against PLANTS). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
